headline: Opportunity Party in kingmaker position as both major leaders' approval slumps
text: The RNZ-Reid Research poll (1,000 respondents, 14–21 Aug, ±3.1% margin) has Labour on 32.2%, National 29.1%, NZ First 11.9%, Greens 10.2%, ACT 7.7%, Opportunity 5.3% and Te Pāti Māori 3.0%. Neither the right bloc (59 seats) nor left bloc (55) could govern without Opportunity's six. Preferred PM sits at Hipkins 21.3%, Luxon 19.9% — a record low for Luxon.

headline: National rules out bed tax and bank tax; mayors say they're "deeply disappointed"
text: PM Christopher Luxon pledged "no new taxes" if re-elected, dropping proposed accommodation ("bed") and bank levies. Finance Minister Nicola Willis said there was no way to apply an accommodation levy without raising costs for Kiwis booking a weekend away. Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown called the move — which walks back a commitment in the Auckland Regional Deal — deeply disappointing.

headline: ACT unveils "one law for all" policy targeting courts and Treaty clauses
text: Leader David Seymour announced a policy to bar courts from treating tikanga as an independent legal source except where Parliament explicitly allows it, and to require Cabinet sign-off on any bill referencing the Treaty of Waitangi. Seymour said recent Supreme Court decisions, including the Ellis case, had "widely expanded the use of tikanga in the law" beyond what Parliament had legislated.

headline: Expelled Te Pāti Māori MP Tākuta Ferris to stand as independent in Te Tai Tonga
text: Ferris, ousted from Te Pāti Māori in late 2025 following internal conflict with party leadership, confirmed he'll contest Te Tai Tonga as an independent candidate rather than rejoining the party he won the seat for in 2023.
